catalog.description: How long a new deposit, exit or consolidation would wait at the current queue length.

method.description: How long a new deposit, exit or consolidation would wait at the current queue length. The wait is what stakers face in practice when they enter or unstake. Waits move with the queues: the churn limit only changes slowly with the size of the stake. Wait = queue / churn limit per epoch, in days of 225 epochs. Entry queue: before the Pectra upgrade (7 May 2025), validators eligible for activation and not yet activated, 32 ETH each, exact for every past epoch from our registry's eligibility and activation epochs; from Pectra, the deposits waiting in the consensus state's deposit queue, read from the full day-end states. Exit queue: validators whose exit has started and whose exit epoch has not been reached; the start is the block that carried its voluntary exit, slashing or execution-layer exit request. Consolidation queue (from Pectra): validators merging into another validator, which wait under their own churn limit. Exit and consolidation amounts are effective balances when the exit started: our registry's value for validators not yet withdrawn, 32 ETH for withdrawn validators with ordinary credentials, and for withdrawn compounding validators their deposits plus the validators merged into them. Churn limits: before Pectra max(4, active validators / 65,536) validators per epoch, with activations capped at 8 per epoch from the Deneb upgrade (13 March 2024); from Pectra min(256 ETH, max(128 ETH, total active balance / 65,536)) per epoch for deposits and exits, and the rest of that balance limit for consolidations. 225 epochs a day. Partial withdrawals requested from the execution layer share the exit churn but are not in the daily history (the hourly readings of the current state include them). Days before our reading of a Pectra-era day-end state show no entry queue. Daily from December 2020. Only finalized blocks and states are used. The open day is a labeled partial, updated hourly, and replaced by the final value once the day closes. Computed by CryptoKeyhole from its own Ethereum execution and consensus nodes. Where a chart uses MEV-Boost relays' published delivery records, each record is matched to the block our own node holds and the amounts come from that block. Periods are UTC.

methodology_breaks.churn_post_pectra: min(256 ETH, max(128 ETH, total active balance / 65,536)) per epoch for deposits and exits; remaining balance churn reserved for consolidations.
methodology_breaks.churn_pre_pectra: max(4, active validators / 65,536) validators per epoch; activations capped at 8 per epoch from Deneb on 2024-03-13.
methodology_breaks.entry_queue_post_pectra: Deposits waiting in the consensus-state deposit queue, read from full day-end states.
methodology_breaks.entry_queue_pre_pectra: Validators eligible for activation and not yet activated, 32 ETH each, reconstructed from registry eligibility and activation epochs.
methodology_breaks.exit_queue: Validators whose exit has started and whose exit epoch has not been reached; includes voluntary exits, slashings and execution-layer exit requests.

methodology_breaks.consolidations: Separate queue and churn limit; not part of the proposed entry-minus-exit feature.
methodology_breaks.partial_withdrawals: Execution-layer-requested partial withdrawals share exit churn but are not in daily history; hourly current-state readings include them.
